niche.habitat: Fumarole slopes, lava tube entrances, hot spring terraces near the stratovolcano
niche.diet: Carcasses, sulfur crusts, basalt grit, mineral seeps

body: Babosa (slug-like crawler) with a vast, insulating dorsal gas-bladder and ventral heat-pads; lacks limbs for walking, moves by clinging and drifting

links: Bladder provides lift in dense air
Hot air density contrast creates buoyancy
Volcanic heat provides constant thermal source

skill.effect: The creature warms its dorsal gas bladder against sun-heated rocks or its own body, causing it to swell and drift slowly downward. It then catches rising air currents to glide through the sky for a short while.

chains.weakness: Wind and cold rapidly cool the bladder, causing immediate loss of lift and a dangerous drop; fire ruptures the bladder.
observe: See creature press ventral pads against hot rock
Watch dorsal frill expand as air is heated
Observe it detach and drift horizontally on rising warm air

journal.en: It doesn't walk. It huffs, heats, and hangs in the air like a rag caught on a thermal.

plausibility.summary: Reframe skill as volcanic assisted soaring: bladder is a large insulated dorsal chamber passively pre-heated on ventral pads; creature achieves partial buoyancy + extended glide on slope thermals (F7), not full unpowered flight. Cap volume ~3–8× body for gameplay; require hot-rock contact to recharge; moonless cold nights (haunting moment) collapse lift—already consistent.
fixes: Reframe skill as volcanic assisted soaring: bladder is a large insulated dorsal chamber passively pre-heated on ventral pads; creature achieves partial buoyancy + extended glide on slope thermals (F7), not full unpowered flight. Cap volume ~3–8× body for gameplay; require hot-rock contact to recharge; moonless cold nights (haunting moment) collapse lift—already consistent.

analogues.organism: Ballooning spiders (e.g. Linyphiidae: silk + wind, not hot-air bladders); Portuguese man-of-war (Physalia: gas float for surface buoyancy, different medium); hang-glider/soarer using ridge thermals (physics only, not homology).

links: Digests toxic sulfur crusts for sulfur and minerals
Symbionts convert H2S/SO2 to usable sulfate and detoxify
Fumarole crusts are poison to most life but abundant
Volcanic gases seep from dyke and tuff fractures

skill.effect: The creature gnaws on sulfur crusts scraped from the ground or fallen carcasses. This nourishes it and drives out any lingering toxins, though raw chunks sometimes make it cough and choke.

chains.weakness: Cannot digest raw sulfur quickly; raw sulfur gifts cause choking damage; gut flora crashes if diet lacks sulfur for too long.
observe: Find missing sulfur crusts near vent
See creature scrape orange crusts with rasping tongue

journal.en: The poison is its pantry. It eats the mountain's breath and breathes back clean air.

plausibility.summary: Fumarole crusts rich in sulfur, SO₂/H₂S (F23) are toxic to generalists (F26) but abundant; specialist scavenger with chemolithotrophic or sulfur-oxidizing gut symbionts is a standard island-radiation niche (F27). Detoxifying vent minerals while eating carcass flesh matches one shared biochemistry (F24). Risk of choking on elemental sulfur without symbiont priming matches slow oxidation kinetics.
fixes: Fumarole crusts rich in sulfur, SO₂/H₂S (F23) are toxic to generalists (F26) but abundant; specialist scavenger with chemolithotrophic or sulfur-oxidizing gut symbionts is a standard island-radiation niche (F27). Detoxifying vent minerals while eating carcass flesh matches one shared biochemistry (F24). Risk of choking on elemental sulfur without symbiont priming matches slow oxidation kinetics.

skill.effect: On wind or attack, inflate bladder instantly and let wind carry away; breaks enemy lock and avoids damage.

chains.weakness: In calm weather or closed caves, it cannot escape; vulnerable to ambush and entrapment.
observe: See creature inflate and blow sideways on threat
Watch it cling to cliff face before drifting
Garfio bites empty air as prey vanishes upwind

journal.en: Fear makes it light. A sudden noise turns it into a balloon.

plausibility.summary: Name effect wind-borne escape: requires minimum wind (game threshold) + partially inflated bladder; does not break predator lock in dead calm or enclosed lava tubes.
fixes: Name effect wind-borne escape: requires minimum wind (game threshold) + partially inflated bladder; does not break predator lock in dead calm or enclosed lava tubes.

links: Efficient heat transfer from rock to bladder
High UV and cold nights demand thermal efficiency

skill.effect: Rests on hot rock to restore bladder heat; passive health regen and lift recovery over time.

chains.weakness: Must find specific hot rocks; cannot use move in water or on cold stone; exposed during rest.
observe: Creature presses flat belly to glowing vent rock
Bladder shrinks as heat is stored in tissue
Thermal pattern shows warm ventral patch

journal.en: It sleeps on the fire, belly to stone, dreaming of the wind.

plausibility.summary: Ectothermic basking on fumarole-heated andesite/basalt (F9, F7) with high conductive heat uptake through ventral surface is sound; insulation limits convective loss in 1.6 bar dense air (F4) and at night/UV-exposed slopes (F14). Links bladder recharge to observable behaviour without violating energy budget if lift is passive storage, not constant metabolic furnacing.
fixes: Ectothermic basking on fumarole-heated andesite/basalt (F9, F7) with high conductive heat uptake through ventral surface is sound; insulation limits convective loss in 1.6 bar dense air (F4) and at night/UV-exposed slopes (F14). Links bladder recharge to observable behaviour without violating energy budget if lift is passive storage, not constant metabolic furnacing.

analogues.organism: Marine iguana (Amblyrhynchus cristatus) ventral basking after cold foraging; many lizards and snakes using sun-warmed rock; deep-sea vent fauna using proton motive force from symbionts while host regulates position near redox gradient.

relations.note: (council kind 'Predator/Prey') Garfio attacks Resoplido at takeoff; Resoplido's drift escape is the only reliable counter to Garfio's charge.
(council kind 'Commensal') Zanco grubs up insects near vents, which Resoplido catches mid-air with its wide throat; Zanco ignores the drifters.
(council kind 'Competition') Both compete for sulfur-mineral carcasses; Espinodo's armor protects Resoplido from smaller scavengers but not from heat.

temperament: Timid, drifts away on updrafts, curled in sleep
secrets: Volcano secret: Flamethrower move (evolved H2S metabolism).
Secret: Eat sulfur crusts to detoxify and unlock sulfur adaptation.
Secret: Found in hidden lava tube near fumaroles.
moments: On moonless nights, when the thermals die, dozens drop from the slopes like stones, curling into ragged knots on the lava flow. You can walk right up to one, thinking it dead, only for a sudden gust to restart its slow, floating wake.

journal.en: El Resoplido. The mountain's ghost. It eats sulfur, sleeps on rock, and lives in the updraft.
Secret: Eat sulfur from carcass. Volcano area. Unlocks H2S resistance and Flamethrower move.
